examples.en: I dried the wet clothes in the sun.
If you dry laundry in a dryer, it dries fast.
Mushrooms are dried and stored for a long time.
Dry your hair completely before you go out.
I like snacks made of dried fruit.

examples.ko: 이 기계는 공기를 건조시키는 기능이 있어요.
examples.en: This machine has a function that dries the air.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 보통 '말리다'를 써요. '건조시키다'는 기계, 식품, 공장 이야기처럼 딱딱한 설명에 어울려요. '날씨가 건조하다'는 형용사 '건조하다'라서 달라요.
explain_en: In everyday talk, '말리다' is the usual word. '건조시키다' suits stiff explanations about machines, food, and factories. '날씨가 건조하다' uses the adjective '건조하다', which is a different word.

examples.en: Every weekend I mop the living room floor with a cloth.
You need to sweep and then wipe the room to get rid of dust.
I scrubbed hard with a cloth, and the floor got clean.

examples.ko: 제가 걸레질할 테니까 청소기를 돌려 주세요.
examples.en: I'll wipe the floor, so please run the vacuum cleaner.

examples.ko: 부엌 바닥은 물걸레로 걸레질하면 잘 닦여요.
examples.en: The kitchen floor gets clean if you wipe it with a wet cloth.
Keep the windows open while you wipe the floor.

explain: 걸레로 바닥이나 가구를 닦는 일이에요. '걸레질을 하다'와 '걸레질하다'를 둘 다 써요. 보통 '쓸기·청소기'로 먼지를 치운 다음에 해요.
explain_en: It is wiping the floor or furniture with a cloth. Both '걸레질을 하다' and '걸레질하다' are used. It usually comes after removing dust by sweeping or vacuuming.

en: piece of wood; block of wood; chunk of wood

examples.en: The child is building a house with wooden blocks.
I gathered pieces of wood to make a fire.
A small piece of wood is rolling around on the floor.
I used a block of wood instead of a chair.
He carved a piece of wood with a knife and made a doll.
I put a piece of wood under the desk leg.

explain: '토막'은 잘라 낸 한 조각을 말해서, 나무토막은 잘려 있는 나무 조각이에요. 불 피울 때 쓰는 나무는 '장작'이라고 해요. 집 짓기 놀이를 하는 장난감 블록도 나무토막이라고 말할 수 있어요.
explain_en: '토막' is a cut-off piece, so a 나무토막 is a piece of wood that has been cut. Wood used for a fire is called '장작'. Wooden toy blocks for building can also be called 나무토막.

examples.en: Please put the leftover side dishes in the fridge compartment.
The fridge compartment door doesn't close properly.
I slowly thaw the meat from the freezer in the fridge compartment.
I lowered the temperature of the fridge compartment a little.

examples.ko: 우유는 냉장실 맨 위 칸에 있어요.
examples.en: The milk is on the top shelf of the fridge compartment.

examples.ko: 냉장실이 꽉 차서 더 못 넣어요.
examples.en: The fridge compartment is full, so I can't put in any more.

explain: 냉장고 안에서 얼리지 않고 차갑게 보관하는 칸을 말하고, 반대는 얼리는 '냉동실'이에요. 일상에서는 그냥 '냉장고'라고 하는 경우가 많아요. 칸을 나눠서 말할 때 냉장실과 냉동실이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the part of the refrigerator that keeps food cold without freezing, and the opposite is the freezer, '냉동실'. In daily speech people often just say '냉장고'. You use 냉장실 and 냉동실 when separating the two compartments.

examples.en: I iron my shirts on Sunday evening.

examples.ko: 면 소재는 다림질하기 전에 물을 살짝 뿌려요.
examples.en: I spray cotton lightly with water before ironing it.
I ironed my suit the day before the interview.
I almost burned my hand while ironing.
The shirt I had ironed got wrinkled again right away.

examples.ko: 시간이 없어서 다림질하지 못하고 그냥 입었어요.
examples.en: I had no time to iron it, so I just wore it as it was.

explain: '옷을 다리다', '다리미질하다'도 같은 뜻으로 많이 말해요. '옷을 다림질하다'처럼 목적어를 붙여 쓰고, 구김을 펴는 일이라 '구겨지다'와 짝으로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: People also say '옷을 다리다' or '다리미질하다' with the same meaning. It takes an object like '옷을 다림질하다', and often appears alongside '구겨지다' (to get wrinkled).

examples.en: I lost the car cover.
The cover was blown away by the wind.

examples.ko: 비가 오니까 덮개로 자전거를 덮어 두세요.
examples.en: It's raining, so put a cover over your bike.

examples.ko: 이 덮개는 세탁기에 빨 수 있어요.
examples.en: This cover can be washed in the washing machine.
If you leave it without a cover, dust builds up.
I need to buy a new chair cover too.

explain: '덮다'에서 나온 말이라서 위에 얹어 가리는 물건에 써요. 냄비나 병을 막는 둥근 것은 보통 '뚜껑'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It comes from the verb 덮다 and is used for something laid over a thing to cover it. The round piece that closes a pot or bottle is usually called 뚜껑.

examples.en: I'll pour you some hot tea in a mug.
My friend gave me a mug as a birthday present.
Can I put this mug in the microwave?

examples.ko: 회사 책상 위에 머그잔이 세 개나 있어요.
examples.en: There are three mugs on my desk at work.
Could you wash just one mug for me?

examples.ko: 손잡이가 달린 머그잔이라서 뜨거워도 들기 편해요.
examples.en: It's a mug with a handle, so it's easy to hold even when hot.

explain: '컵'은 더 넓게 쓰는 말이고, '머그잔'은 손잡이가 달린 큼직한 잔을 말해요. '머그컵'이라고도 해요. 마시는 것에 따라 '찻잔', '커피잔'처럼도 부르고, 잔을 세는 말은 '개'를 써요.
explain_en: '컵' is the broader word, while '머그잔' is a large cup with a handle. People also say '머그컵'. Depending on what you drink you may also say '찻잔' or '커피잔', and you count cups with '개'.

examples.en: I folded the clothes and put them in the dresser.

examples.ko: 문구류는 따로 신청하지 말고 서랍장에서 필요한 만큼 가져가세요.
examples.en: Don't request stationery separately; take what you need from the drawer chest.

examples.ko: 방이 좁아서 서랍장을 놓을 자리가 없어요.
examples.en: The room is small, so there's no space to put a chest of drawers.

examples.ko: 서랍장 맨 아래 칸이 잘 안 열려요.
examples.en: The bottom drawer of the chest won't open easily.
I heard the new chest of drawers is being delivered today.

examples.ko: 이 서랍장은 칸이 다섯 개나 돼서 편해요.
examples.en: This chest has as many as five drawers, so it's convenient.

explain: '서랍'은 열고 닫는 칸 하나를 말하고, '서랍장'은 그런 칸이 여러 개 있는 가구예요. 옷을 걸어 두는 '옷장'과 달리 접은 옷이나 작은 물건을 넣어요. 칸을 셀 때는 '칸'이나 '단'으로 말해요.
explain_en: '서랍' is a single sliding drawer, while '서랍장' is the piece of furniture with several of them. Unlike a '옷장' where you hang clothes, you keep folded clothes and small items in it. You count the drawers with '칸' or '단'.

examples.en: A button came off, so I fixed it temporarily with a safety pin.
Is there a safety pin in your bag?
The skirt waist was loose, so I put in a safety pin.
I pricked my finger on a safety pin and it hurt.
I found a few safety pins in the drawer.
After using a safety pin, keep it closed.

explain: 옷을 임시로 고정하거나 이름표를 달 때 쓰는 작은 핀이에요. 머리에 꽂는 '머리핀'과는 쓰임이 달라요. 찔리기 쉬우니 '찔리다', '꽂다', '닫다'와 같이 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is a small pin used to hold clothes temporarily or attach a name tag. It's different from a '머리핀' (hairpin). People often use it with verbs like '찔리다' (get pricked), '꽂다' (pin in) and '닫다' (close).

examples.en: I put the homemade jam in a glass jar.
Glass bottles break easily if you drop them.

examples.ko: 집에 빈 유리병을 많이 모아 두었어요.
examples.en: I have collected lots of empty glass bottles at home.
I put barley tea in a glass bottle in the fridge.

examples.ko: 이 유리병 뚜껑이 너무 꽉 닫혀서 안 열려요.
examples.en: This glass jar's lid is on so tight that it won't open.
I put finished glass bottles in the recycling bin.

explain: 분리수거 때 '유리병', '페트병', '캔'으로 나눠서 버려요. 유리병은 '깨지다', '깨뜨리다'와 자주 같이 나와요. 잼을 담는 병도 유리병이고, 꽃을 꽂는 병은 '꽃병'이라고 따로 불러요.
explain_en: When sorting recycling, Koreans separate 'yuribyeong' (glass bottles), 'petbyeong' (plastic bottles) and cans. Because glass breaks, it often comes with '깨지다' (break) and '깨뜨리다' (break something). A jar for jam is also a yuribyeong, but a bottle for flowers has its own name, '꽃병' (vase).

en: wardrobe; large closet for clothes and bedding

examples.en: I put the blanket away in the wardrobe.

examples.ko: 장롱이 너무 커서 방이 좁아 보여요.
examples.en: The wardrobe is so big that the room looks small.
Moving the wardrobe was hard when we moved house.
Grandmother's room also has an old wardrobe.

examples.ko: 옷을 장롱에 걸어 두면 구겨지지 않아요.
examples.en: If you hang clothes in the wardrobe, they won't wrinkle.

examples.ko: 장롱은 보통 방 한쪽 벽에 놓아요.
examples.en: A wardrobe is usually placed against one wall of the room.

explain: '옷장'은 옷을 넣는 가구이고, '장롱'은 옷뿐 아니라 이불 같은 것도 넣어 두는 크고 튼튼한 가구예요. 옷 넣는 용도를 말하고 싶으면 '옷장'이라고 하면 돼요.
explain_en: 옷장 is furniture for clothes, while 장롱 is a large, sturdy piece of furniture that holds bedding such as blankets as well as clothes. If you want to stress that it is for clothes, you can say 옷장.

examples.en: I fitted new tires on the car.
A drone fitted with a camera flies in the sky.

examples.ko: 휴대폰에 케이스를 장착하는 데 일 분도 안 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes less than a minute to put a case on the phone.

examples.ko: 이 의자에는 바퀴를 장착할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can attach wheels to this chair.
I mounted a light on my bike and rode at night.
Try fitting it slowly while following the manual.

explain: '달다', '끼우다'보다 딱딱한 말이라서 기계·부품·장비 이야기에 어울려요. 보통 '~에 ~을 장착하다' 모양으로 써요. 게임에서 장비를 몸에 갖출 때도 '장착하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is more formal than '달다' or '끼우다' and suits talk about machines, parts, and gear. It usually takes the pattern '~에 ~을 장착하다'. In games, equipping an item is also called '장착하다'.

examples.en: A lot of dust has piled up on the window frame.
When it rains, water collects in the window frame.
The cat is sitting on the window sill.
I brought a rag to wipe the window frame.
The window frame is old, so the wind comes in.
I put the flowerpot on the window ledge.

explain: 유리가 아니라 창을 둘러싼 틀 부분이에요. 대청소할 때 '창틀 청소'가 힘들다는 말을 많이 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the frame around the window, not the glass. People often say that cleaning the window frames is the hard part of a big clean.

examples.en: This insurance covers hospital bills.
I covered my gray hair with a hat.
I will cover that work for you.

examples.ko: 이 앱 하나로 모든 기능을 커버할 수 있어요.
examples.en: This one app can cover every function.
I tried to hide the blemish with makeup.
My friend covered for my mistake.

explain: '가리다'는 눈에 안 보이게 덮는 것이고, '커버하다'는 가리는 것 말고도 대신 메우거나 범위를 포함하는 뜻까지 넓게 써요. 회사에서 '제가 커버할게요'는 '제가 대신 맡을게요'라는 말로 자주 나와요. 다른 가수의 노래를 다시 부르는 것도 '커버하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: 가리다 is to cover something so it can't be seen, while 커버하다 goes further to mean filling in for someone or including a range. At work, 제가 커버할게요 often means 'I'll take over for you'. Singing another artist's song is also called 커버하다.

examples.en: I laminate the paper so it won't tear.
Yesterday I laminated my student ID.
I will laminate this poster tomorrow.
Laminating takes about five minutes.
I laminated the photo and stuck it on the wall.

examples.ko: 비에 젖지 않도록 코팅해서 쓰고 있어요.
examples.en: I coat it so it doesn't get wet in the rain, and I use it.

explain: 종이를 비닐로 싸는 일에도, 프라이팬이나 안경 렌즈 겉에 막을 입히는 일에도 써요. 이미 처리된 물건은 '코팅된 종이'처럼 '코팅되다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It is used both for sealing paper in plastic and for putting a layer on the surface of a frying pan or eyeglass lens. A finished item is described with 코팅되다, as in 코팅된 종이.

examples.en: I bought a new mouse pad.
It is a jacket with pads in the shoulders.
I put on knee pads, too, and went skating.
This pad is soft, so it is comfortable to sit on.
Thanks to the pad, the chair is soft.
Water got on the pad, so I wiped it.

explain: 패드는 부드럽게 대거나 받치는 물건에 두루 쓰이는 외래어예요. '마우스 패드', '무릎 패드'처럼 앞말이 무엇인지 알려 줘요. 겨울에 입는 두꺼운 옷은 '패딩'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 패드 is a loanword for soft things placed against or under something. The word in front tells you which kind, as in '마우스 패드' and '무릎 패드'. The thick padded winter jacket is called '패딩'.
